plain: To make something less severe or harmful

webster.text: To alleviate, as suffering; to assuage; to lessen; as, to mitigate pain or grief.

more.text: To temper; to moderate; to soften in harshness or severity.
To calm; to appease; to moderate; as, to mitigate the fierceness of party.
To diminish; to render more tolerable; as, to mitigate the evils or calamities of life; to mitigate punishment.
To reduce in amount or severity; as, to mitigate a penalty.

example.quote: And there being constant danger of excess, the effort ought to be by force of public opinion, to mitigate and assuage it.
